2.text: The shamanistic “spirits” are very ill tempered, especially toward the

3.text: shaman with whom they are connected. If he does not carry out implicitly

4.text: all the suggestions they make about his dress, mode of living, and the details

5.text: of ceremonials, they become angry and chastise him, or punish him otherwise.

6.text: If he continues to disobey, they kill him. If the “spirits” are displeased with

7.text: any of the listeners at a ceremony, they usually take vengeance on the

8.text: shaman. For this reason, outsiders must be very quiet, and careful not to

9.text: pry into the work of the “spirits.”

10.text: On the other hand, when the shaman has kept faithfully his compact

11.text: with the “spirits,” they must come at his call, and must assist him in all

12.text: troubles and difficulties. “These are my people, my own little ‘spirits,’” said

13.text: one shaman when I expressed a doubt as to whether his “spirits” would come

14.text: or not. “They will not leave me, but will seek me all the time, as a fawn

36.text: Shamanistic “spirits,” as a rule, do not like one another. When they
